---
title: "Quiz · Inside a Sandcastle"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you
can self-grade after answering.

## 1. Which academy layer does a Sandcastle occupy?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **construction** layer. Crossplane occupies the **composition**
layer (what should exist), Sandcastle occupies the **construction**
layer (how a new artifact is safely produced), and Pico occupies the
**behaviour** layer (what the resulting entity does at runtime).
:::

## 2. What are the five construction-layer concerns a Sandcastle addresses?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
1. **Isolated workspaces** — the sandbox boundary.
2. **Repo/branch flow** — how work moves in and out durably.
3. **Tools and permissions** — what the engineering agent can and
   cannot do.
4. **Agent iteration** — the inspect → generate → validate → commit
   inner loop.
5. **Artifact boundaries** — only committed Git content crosses out.
:::

## 3. Why is it safe to dispose of a Sandcastle after it finishes?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Because the artifact boundary guarantees that **only** committed Git
content (a branch on the target repository, and optionally a PR)
crosses out of the Sandcastle. The workspace, tools, and any agent
scratch state are all disposable — nothing engineering-relevant is
lost when the sandbox is torn down.
:::

## 4. If the agent's inner iteration loop fails validation, what happens next?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The loop **repeats inside the Sandcastle**: the agent diagnoses the
failure and revises the files in the same isolated workspace on the
same branch. The surrounding delivery pipeline (PR, merge, GitOps,
Crossplane reconciliation) never sees the failed attempts.
:::

## 5. Why does the Sandcastle course not yet include a runnable Sandcastle lab, and where will one live when it does?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
This wave of the course delivers substantive **instruction** but
intentionally defers a runnable Sandcastle lab to a later
curriculum-verification wave. When a runnable lab lands it will live
as a reusable lab under the repository-root `labs/` directory (for
example, `labs/hello-world-pico-sandcastle/`) — the same convention
used by [Hello Pico](../../../../labs/hello-pico/) and
[Hello Pico on Kubernetes](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/)
— so it can be reused across courses.
:::
